disclaimer: Internal design rubric (1–5 per criterion, weighted to 100). Not a CTR prediction.

rubric.label: Mobile legibility
rubric.ask: Can the text and focal point be read at 320x180 in a feed?

rubric.label: Curiosity & clarity
rubric.ask: Is there a clear question or tension a viewer wants resolved, without confusion?

rubric.label: Focal hierarchy
rubric.ask: Is there one immediately identifiable focal point, then text, then supporting detail?

rubric.label: Subject isolation
rubric.ask: Does the subject separate cleanly from the background (edge, contrast, light)?

rubric.label: Visual uniqueness
rubric.ask: Does it stand apart from the reference thumbnails instead of copying them?

rubric.label: Title/thumbnail synergy
rubric.ask: Does the image add information the title does not repeat?

rubric.label: Authenticity & accuracy
rubric.ask: Is every claim, result and graphic true to the video? Real face, real evidence?

rubric.label: Brand consistency
rubric.ask: Does it feel like AI with Kalyan (coral accent, dark tech, clean type) without being a clone of the others?

rows.headline: RAW → EDITED
rows.verdict: Strong proof concept. The raw camera frame vs the finished edit's real 25/25 QA screen tells the story in one glance. Two big labels read at 320 px.

rows.headline: I DIDN'T EDIT THIS
rows.verdict: Most human and emotionally direct. A real raised-brow expression, coral rim light and a true four-word claim that the title resolves.

rows.headline: › edit my video
rows.verdict: Cleanest and lowest-entropy design: one command line, one real filmstrip. Unmissable at feed size, but it repeats the title's idea rather than adding to it.

rows.headline: WHO EDITED THIS?
rows.verdict: Best curiosity gap: 'Who edited this?' is answered by the title. Face, card and question compete for first look.

rows.headline: RAW → DONE
rows.verdict: Explains the 'how' with verifiable proof. The revision made the result card dominant and the proof badge readable.
